bullets.text: Nuvama sees Hindustan Zinc 2QFY27 EBITDA Rs84.2bn (+5% QoQ), 0.6% below street; PAT Rs57.5bn vs street Rs55.9bn; reports Mon 14:00.
bullets.source: Nuvama — Result Estimates for 19th October 2026: BAF, UTCEM, HZ, UNBK

detail.summary: Nuvama expects EBITDA to rise on higher average zinc, partly offset by weaker silver and lead. Margin is seen at 59.5% against street 60.3%. Futures show shorts present and rollover below its average.
points: Lead vol +8.5%, silver +16% QoQ; zinc flat

bullets.text: Emkay: zinc keeps bearish bias as LME stocks top 150kt; aluminium bounces toward $3,000/t from $2,953 with MCX backwardation widening to Rs1.45/kg.
bullets.source: Emkay — Commodity Market Report: Precious metals rebound as dollar weakens, crude inventories tighten

detail.summary: Base metals attempt a recovery after two down sessions, with the dollar easing toward 102. Zinc is the weak link on rising inventories, while aluminium looks oversold with near-term tightness in the domestic spread. FOMC on 27-28 Oct is the next macro trigger.

bullets.text: Morgan Stanley: India HRC at Rs63.8K/t, ~1% lower WoW but +11% since July, a ~5% premium to import parity; sees limited near-term upside.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley — PULSE: India Materials: India Steel Tracker

detail.summary: Imports have been elevated as domestic output slowed and inventories depleted. With prices above import parity, upside is limited, but the safeguard duty keeps spreads supported into the seasonally strong period. Industry view In-Line; constructive on steel stocks' outperformance.
points: Secondary rebar Rs51.8K/t, -2% WoW, +18% since July
Steel stocks flat YTD vs Sensex -13%

bullets.text: Elara: covered cement stocks trade below 5-year EV/t lows, Shree and Ambuja at decade lows; prefers Shree, accumulate gradually as margins stay pressured.
bullets.source: Elara — Cement - Looking beyond near-term headwinds - Sector Update

detail.summary: Elara values cement on normalised earnings (5-year average EBITDA/tonne, FY29E volumes) because fuel-cost normalisation is uncertain. Elevated petcoke and coal keep margins under pressure but could prompt further price hikes; estimates retained until Q2FY27 results.
points: Utilisation flat ~72-73%; West & Central oversupply risk
Shree top large-cap pick; Birla Corp small-cap pick

bullets.text: Nuvama expects UltraTech Q2 (Mon 19 Oct, ~14:00) EBITDA Rs37.96bn vs street 37.01bn; core PAT Rs16.99bn vs 16.04bn, with volumes ~+11% YoY.
bullets.source: Nuvama — Result Estimates for 19th October 2026: BAF, UTCEM, HZ, UNBK

detail.summary: Nuvama sits modestly above Bloomberg consensus on UltraTech, but flags blended EBITDA/t likely to decline on cost pressure. Derivatives show legacy shorts largely covered after delivery-based selling on 1 Oct.
points: Rollover 92% vs 96% prev expiry; 11500CE peak OI

bullets.text: Avendus Spark sees India Cements Q2 (Sat 17 Oct) EBITDA Rs1.10bn vs consensus Rs0.81bn, sales Rs10.57bn vs 11.17bn; flags it among six-month consensus downgrades.
bullets.source: Avendus Spark — Results Oct 16-17; Last 6M Earnings - Upgrades ...; Downgrades - India Cements

detail.summary: Spark's India Cements estimate is above Bloomberg on EBITDA but below on sales. Consensus FY27 estimates for the company have been cut over the past six months.
points: 6M consensus FY27 change: sales -13%, EBITDA +6%, PAT -14%

bullets.text: Memory chips are ~40% of budget-handset BoM; with prices surging, Ai+, Lava, Mivi and Boltt push sub-Rs15,000 phones while Samsung, Oppo, Vivo and Xiaomi retreat.
bullets.source: Nomura — India Consumer Durables and EMS: Homegrown firms enter budget smartphone market as memory chip prices rise

detail.summary: Memory-chip inflation has raised entry-level smartphone production costs sharply, and global brands are cutting exposure to the segment. Local brands are filling the gap, helped by the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme incentives.
points: Memory ~40% of budget-phone bill of materials
Noise, boAt, GoBoult exploring sub-Rs15,000 entry via e-commerce
Samsung, Oppo, Vivo, Xiaomi reducing entry-level exposure

bullets.text: LTM 2QFY27 EBIT margin 15.6% missed Emkay's 15.8%; TCV $1.26bn (~1.0x book-to-bill); FY27E EPS cut 6.4%, ADD kept, TP Rs4,450.
bullets.source: Emkay — LTM: Margin miss; soft order inflow; ADD; Target: Rs4,450

detail.summary: Revenue was in line at +1.1% cc but margin and order intake disappointed. Management targets FY27 growth and margins roughly flat on FY26 with 2H acceleration, leaning on AI-led deals that are short-tenure. Emkay trims FY27 EPS on the miss and higher forex losses, leaves FY28-29 largely unchanged.
points: TP Rs4,450 at 18x Sep-28E EPS; CMP Rs4,385

bullets.text: Wipro Q3 guide of -1.5% to +0.5% cc and TCV $2.6bn (-45% yoy) disappoint; PhillipCapital stays Neutral, TP Rs180, FY27 EPS cut 3%.
bullets.source: PhillipCapital — Wipro (WPRO IN) - Weak TCV and Guidance; Continues to Underperform

detail.summary: Q2 revenue and margin were slightly better than feared, but fourth straight yoy fall in total and large-deal TCV and furlough-hit Q3 guidance signal weak pipeline conversion. Phillip expects FY27 to be a fourth year of revenue decline and Wipro to lag peers, with 12x FY28 valuation limiting downside.
points: IT services flat qoq cc; EBIT margin 16.4-16.5%
Mgmt expects growth positive from Q4

bullets.text: IIFL upgrades Tech Mahindra to BUY (TP Rs2,000) on 2.4% cc growth, 14.8% EBIT margin, $1bn+ deals; downgrades Wipro to REDUCE (TP Rs160).
bullets.source: IIFL Sales — Tech Mahindra upgraded to BUY, TP ₹2,000 | Wipro downgraded to REDUCE, TP ₹160 (+9 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: IIFL sees the TechM turnaround nearing completion with growth leadership and re-rating potential, raising EPS 5-10%. On Wipro it sees flat revenue, weak TCV and falling headcount with limited valuation comfort versus TCS and Infosys.
points: TechM TP Rs2,000 from Rs1,750, +21% upside
TechM FY27-29 revenue CAGR 7%, EPS CAGR 14%
Wipro TP Rs160 from Rs165, 8% downside

bullets.text: Nifty gained 2.8% on the week, sharpest since April, as IT jumped 11.7% (18-year best) while Korea fell 16.2% and Taiwan 4.5% on AI-trade fears.

detail.summary: India was the best-performing market in a regional tech sell-off, but the rally was a short-covering style move: FIIs kept selling and sentiment stays in the bearish zone. Valuations rose with bond yields, widening the yield gap.
points: FII outflows US$0.8bn on week; CY26-TD US$32.7bn
INR +1.9% vs USD on RBI measures
Nifty 12m fwd PE 17.1x; bond-earnings yield gap 1.55ppt
Bull-Bear index 27.3% bullish vs 8.9% a week ago

bullets.text: FIIs bought futures in size after the prior day's selling and DIIs bought US$590mn; Kotak sees support for Nifty to clear 23,000.
bullets.source: Kotak — sales note: FII turn size buyers in futures

detail.summary: Kotak's flow read says the reversal in FII futures positioning puts large-cap positioning trends back in the positive zone. Overnight cues were supportive; retail cut index longs sharply.
points: FII cash+futures net flow flattish; DII bought US$590mn
Retail cut US$1.56bn of composite index longs
Retail net sold US$296mn of single-stock futures

bullets.text: BofA Bull & Bear indicator fell to 7.4, ending the May 26 sell signal; BofA stays risk-off until post-US midterms and sees bond yields falling further.
bullets.source: BofA — The Flow Show: Sell Signal Ends (+9 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Extreme bull sentiment has unwound, though allocators are not underweight risk given record 2026 inflows. BofA expects falling yields to improve equity breadth in Q4 and favours peak-yield exposure and consumer.
points: INR near all-time lows; -21% over five years
Tech fund inflows record, US$196bn annualised

bullets.text: Kotak lifts FY27E domestic M&HCV growth to 10-11% yoy from 5-6%; upgrades Ashok Leyland to BUY (FV Rs180), keeps TMCV BUY (FV Rs500).
bullets.source: Kotak — Automobiles & Components: M&HCV demand remains firm; operator profitability holds

detail.summary: 1HFY27 retail momentum, steady freight and healthy utilisation drive the upgrade; operators have passed costs through via higher freight rates. Growth should moderate in 2HFY27 on a high base. EBITDA estimates cut 1-3% on commodity headwinds.
points: CV RM basket +25% vs 3QFY26; 3% price hike taken
TMCV and AL FY27-29 EBITDA cut 1-3%

bullets.text: CLSA: 1H Oct retail stable MoM but down sharply YoY on festive timing; dealers still guide mid-to-high single-digit festive growth; M&M top pick, then Bajaj, Ather.
bullets.source: CLSA — India autos: Auto pulse check: All eyes on festive

detail.summary: YoY decline reflects last year's GST-cut pent-up base and an inauspicious buying period spilling into early October. Channel checks show healthy Dussehra inquiries and largely normal inventory, with some entry-level elasticity after price hikes.

bullets.text: Crompton 2QFY27: revenue +18% yoy beat, EBITDA +24%; Kotak calls it 8% ahead, Avendus sees 9.0% margin and PAT 9.5% below its estimate.
bullets.source: Kotak — Crompton Greaves Consumer (Rs216, BUY) 2QFY27 first cut; Avendus — Crompton 2QFY27 Snapshot (+5 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Both houses see revenue beating, led by ECD, but differ on profit versus their own models. Gross margin fell on raw-material inflation, offset in Kotak's read by lower A&P spend. Kotak will revisit estimates after the 5pm call.
points: Avendus: EBITDA Rs2.05bn, 8% below; adj PAT Rs1.19bn, +30% yoy
Working capital 22 days vs 14; operating cash flow -Rs2.3bn

ai_semis.text: SOX -3.83%, AMD -5.95%, Broadcom -4.52%, TSMC ADR -2.28%, Nvidia -1.43%; Nasdaq -2.15% in the 16 Oct US close.
UBS: APAC tech de-risked Thursday, Kospi -16% week to date, Taiwan US$9.9bn foreign outflows; crowded positioning limits buying to short covering.
ai_semis.source: UBS — TECH PRICE ACTION - APAC TECH SELL OFF | Semis Monthly

ai_semis.text: UBS calls the 19% memory pullback from September's peak an entry point on server DDR5 demand; Samsung Electronics stays top pick.
ai_semis.source: UBS — TECH PRICE ACTION - APAC TECH SELL OFF | Semis Monthly
